questions.question_text: The daily maximum temperature, in $^{\circ}$C, was recorded for six days: $34$, $35$, $33$, $36$, $35$, $17$. Which temperature is the outlier?

options.why: Chose the largest value, but an outlier is the value far from the rest, not the maximum.
Chose the most frequent temperature (the mode) instead of the value far from the rest.
Gave the range, $36-17$, instead of naming the outlying temperature.

questions.solution_text:
$17, 33, 34, 35, 35, 36$
The outlier is $17^{\circ}$C, because it is much lower than every other temperature.

options.why: Named the largest price inside the group of close prices instead of the isolated price.
Named the smallest price, but here the isolated price is much higher, not lower, than the rest.
Named a price from the middle of the cluster instead of the value far from the rest.

questions.solution_text:
$400, 450, 500, 550, 600, 1000$
The outlier is $1000$, because it is much higher than the other five prices.

questions.question_text: The heights, in metres, of seven trees in a park are $5.1$, $5.3$, $5.4$, $5.6$, $8.2$, $11.0$ and $14.5$. Where is the cluster?

options.why: Gave the full spread of the data instead of the group of values bunched together.
Named the three widely separated heights as a cluster, but they are far apart.
Named the empty interval after the bunched values, which is the gap rather than the cluster.

questions.solution_text:
$5.1, 5.3, 5.4, 5.6, 8.2, 11.0, 14.5$
Four heights lie between $5.1$ m and $5.6$ m, so the cluster is from $5.1$ m to $5.6$ m.

options.why: Gave the full spread of the prices instead of the interval that contains no data.
Named a step between two neighbouring prices inside the cluster, where there is no empty interval.
Chose the interval between the two highest prices, which is only $50$ wide, rather than the large empty interval.

questions.solution_text:
$200, 250, 300, 350, 600, 650, 700$
There is a gap between $350$ and $600$, because no unit is priced in that interval.

questions.question_text: The daily maximum temperature, in $^{\circ}$C, was recorded for six days: $21$, $24$, $27$, $30$, $33$, $36$. Which statement about this dataset is correct?

options.text: There is no outlier, because the temperatures rise in equal steps of $3^{\circ}$C.
$36^{\circ}$C is an outlier, because it is the highest temperature.
options.why: Treats the largest value as automatically an outlier, but an outlier must sit far from the rest.

options.text: $21^{\circ}$C is an outlier, because it is the lowest temperature.
options.why: Treats the smallest value as automatically an outlier, but an outlier must sit far from the rest.

options.text: $36^{\circ}$C is an outlier, because the spread of $15^{\circ}$C is large.
options.why: Uses a wide spread as evidence of an outlier, but an even spread has no value far from the rest.

questions.solution_text:
$21, 24, 27, 30, 33, 36$
Each temperature is $3^{\circ}$C above the one before, so no temperature sits far from the rest and there is no outlier.

questions.question_text: Each dataset below gives the heights, in metres, of five trees in a park. Which dataset contains an outlier?

options.why: The heights rise by $1$ m each time, so no height sits far from the rest.
Chose a dataset with a wide spread, but the heights are evenly spaced and none is far from the rest.
Chose a dataset with a gap, but each side of the gap holds several heights, so no single height stands alone.

questions.solution_text:
$8, 9, 10, 11, 30$
The height $30$ m is $19$ m above the next highest, while the other four heights are within $3$ m of each other, so $30$ m is the outlier.

options.why: Named the lowest temperature, but here the isolated value is much higher, not lower, than the rest.
Named the highest temperature inside the closely grouped days instead of the isolated day.
Named the most frequent temperature (the mode) instead of the value far from the rest.

questions.solution_text:
$18, 18, 20, 20, 20, 22, 22, 36$
The outlier is $36^{\circ}$C, recorded on day $6$, because it is much higher than the other seven temperatures.

options.text: The heights cluster from $3$ m to $7$ m, there is a gap from $7$ m to $18$ m, and $18$ m is an outlier.
The heights cluster from $3$ m to $18$ m, and there is no outlier.
options.why: Treats the whole spread as one cluster and ignores the height standing far from the others.

options.text: The heights cluster from $3$ m to $7$ m, there is a gap from $7$ m to $18$ m, and $3$ m is an outlier.
options.why: Names the smallest height as the outlier, but $3$ m sits inside the cluster.

options.text: There is a gap from $3$ m to $7$ m, and the heights cluster from $7$ m to $18$ m.
options.why: Swaps the meanings of cluster and gap: the bunched values form the cluster and the empty interval is the gap.

questions.solution_text:
$3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 18$
Five heights lie between $3$ m and $7$ m, so that is the cluster.
No tree has a height between $7$ m and $18$ m, so that interval is a gap.
The outlier is $18$ m, because it is much higher than the rest.
